phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Symbolic execution analysis confirms the validation ordering is CORRECT. All cheap structural checks (ValidFields, CorrectSubnet, time-based checks) are performed before expensive cryptographic operations (ValidProposerSignature, SidecarInclusionProven, SidecarKzgProofVerified). No counterexample path exists where expensive operations execute before structural validation. The implementation follows the spec-mandated ordering and provides effective DoS resistance.

symbolic_analysis.approach: Performed control flow analysis with symbolic input variables to identify all possible execution paths through the validation pipeline. Analyzed computational complexity of each validation step and ordering constraints.

path_conditions.cost: O(n) where n = message size, but occurs BEFORE any crypto

O(1) - string comparison and subnet calculation

path_conditions.note: Expensive but occurs after crypto verifications

scenario_1_invalid_index.description: Attacker sends sidecar with index >= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS

scenario_2_zero_commitments.description: Attacker sends sidecar with empty kzg_commitments array

scenario_3_too_many_commitments.description: Attacker sends sidecar with more commitments than max_blobs_per_block

scenario_4_length_mismatch.description: Attacker sends sidecar where len(column) != len(commitments) or len(proofs)

scenario_5_invalid_signature.description: Attacker sends structurally valid sidecar with forged signature
scenario_5_invalid_signature.expected_cost: O(1) structural checks + O(sig_verify) - rejected at ValidProposerSignature (stage 6, line 126)
scenario_5_invalid_signature.reason: Passes structural checks but signature verification acts as cost gate. Attacker pays O(sig_verify) which is expensive but necessary. This is the INTENDED cost barrier.

scenario_6_invalid_inclusion_proof.description: Attacker sends structurally valid sidecar with valid signature but invalid inclusion proof
scenario_6_invalid_inclusion_proof.reason: Requires valid BLS signature which attacker cannot forge without proposer key. Cost gate protects inclusion proof verification.

scenario_7_invalid_kzg_proof.description: Attacker sends structurally valid sidecar with valid signature and inclusion proof but invalid KZG proof
scenario_7_invalid_kzg_proof.expected_cost: Full validation cost including KZG verification
scenario_7_invalid_kzg_proof.reason: Requires both valid signature AND valid inclusion proof. Attacker cannot reach KZG verification without proposer key.

cost_asymmetry_analysis.defender_cost_with_ordering: O(1) for structurally invalid sidecars, O(sig_verify) minimum for valid structure
cost_asymmetry_analysis.reasoning: By placing O(1) structural checks before O(kzg) crypto checks, the implementation prevents attackers from amplifying their O(1) effort into O(kzg) defender cost

satisfiability_analysis.sat_solver_approach: Control flow analysis with constraint propagation
constraints: C1: ValidFields() must execute before ValidProposerSignature()
C2: ValidFields() must execute before SidecarInclusionProven()
C3: ValidFields() must execute before SidecarKzgProofVerified()
C4: ValidProposerSignature() must execute before SidecarKzgProofVerified()
C5: CorrectSubnet() must execute before expensive operations
C6: All temporal checks must execute before expensive operations
satisfiability_analysis.result: UNSAT - no satisfying assignment exists for the negation
satisfiability_analysis.proof: Sequential code execution with early returns ensures all structural checks (lines 77-99) complete before any expensive operation (lines 126-149). The control flow graph has no path from entry to expensive operations that bypasses structural checks.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The validateDataColumn function is directly reachable from untrusted network peers via pubsub gossip. However, the property is SATISFIED: attackers cannot trigger expensive operations without first passing cheap structural validation. The implementation provides effective defense-in-depth against DoS attacks targeting validation cost asymmetry.

entry_points.name: Gossip Subscription
entry_points.description: Data column sidecars received over gossip p2p network are validated by this function

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.data_flow_path: untrusted_peer → gossip_message → decodePubsubMessage → DataColumnSidecar → RODataColumn → RODataColumnsVerifier → validation_sequence

validation_layers.name: Structural Validation (CRITICAL DEFENSE)
checks: ValidFields: index bounds, zero commitments, max blobs, length consistency
validation_layers.bypassed_if: NEVER - all sidecars must pass these O(1) checks

validation_layers.name: Cryptographic Cost Gate
validation_layers.bypassed_if: attacker has proposer private key (trusted actor)
validation_layers.note: This is the INTENDED cost barrier - only structurally valid sidecars reach here

validation_layers.name: KZG Proof Validation
validation_layers.bypassed_if: attacker has valid signature and inclusion proof
validation_layers.note: Most expensive operation, protected by multiple layers

effective_defenses: Structural validation (Layer 3) provides O(1) rejection before O(kzg) operations
Signature verification (Layer 4) acts as cost gate before expensive proofs
Sequential ordering enforced by early returns prevents bypass

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.notes: Property PROP-W4B13-58 is SATISFIED. The implementation correctly orders validation checks to prevent DoS attacks. Structural validation (O(1)) occurs at lines 77-99 before any expensive operations. The first expensive operation is signature verification at line 126, which serves as the intended cost gate. Subsequent expensive operations (inclusion proof at line 142, KZG proof at line 147) are protected by this gate. An attacker cannot trigger O(kzg) operations without first passing O(1) structural checks and O(sig) signature verification. The defense-in-depth architecture is sound.
